task: Add `codemie analytics sync install|run|status|uninstall` to codemie-code: per-OS daily scheduler (launchd/systemd user timer/Task Scheduler), marker+lookback webhook delivery identical to the standalone collector, status view, uninstall, take-over of standalone installs, and a safe non-interactive scheduled CLI start.

key_reasoning.reason: Base L: a new `analytics sync` sub-tree under the analytics command (install with per-OS scheduler registration, run orchestration with marker and lookback, status, uninstall with take-over of standalone jobs) plus a narrow change to the CLI bootstrap (bin/codemie.js update check) and attachment naming. That is 4+ components across the CLI command, analytics domain and bootstrap areas. Bumped to XL because webhook delivery is a new external integration for codemie-code. The shared-utility flag was not applied separately: the bootstrap and slug changes are small, env-gated touches already covered by the L criterion 'shared utilities involved'.

Base L: codemie-code has no scheduler, webhook or marker precedent. The closest pattern is the tested standalone collector in codemie-onboarding, which is ported rather than reused. Platform-specific registration (launchd bootstrap, systemd user timer with linger, UTF-16 schtasks XML) can only be partly tested off-platform. A scheduled CLI start must suppress update checks and prompts, and the Windows .cmd shim needs CVE-2024-27980-safe quoting. Bumped to XL for security: the webhook sig is the endpoint's whole authorization and must be masked in status, logs and errors, and the settings file must be mode 600. The edge-case test bump was not applied because the collector's node:test suites (scheduler, collect, marker, lookback, webhook, install-args) give ready-made case lists for the enumerated error paths. Take-over keeps the existing ~/.codemie state files in their current format and only replaces the OS job, so it is not scored as a data migration.

About 8-12 new source modules under src/cli/commands/analytics/collector/ (scheduler generators and registration, marker, lookback, webhook, run, install args, identity, status, uninstall/take-over) with matching Vitest files. About 6-8 modified files: analytics/index.ts, the runAnalytics export path or report naming, bin/codemie.js, possibly cli-updater/paths, and docs/COMMANDS.md plus ANALYTICS-REPORT.md. These span src, bin and docs. The new-file count reaches the XXL threshold, but the modified count and the confinement to one command sub-tree fit XL.

Base L: CLI command surface, service logic (run orchestration, window computation), persistence (mode-600 settings, last-sent marker and run log under CODEMIE_HOME), and infrastructure (OS schedulers and the CLI bootstrap path). Bumped to XL for the External layer added by the outbound webhook POST through the system proxy dispatcher.

The story is approved with detailed acceptance criteria for every subcommand, recorded decisions D1-D10 (take-over, no updates in scheduled runs, email required, lowercase slug, delivery contract) and no open questions. Minor implementation details remain: a stable node/codemie job target when version managers are used, and how the bootstrap detects a scheduled run.

Agrees with the project L anchor profile-provider-decoupling (total 23: XL scope, L risk, XXL files). This task has higher risk and layer spread from the OS scheduler and webhook surfaces, lower clarity cost, and a similar total.
